bc_mount_land.blurb: Mount Land is a steep rock spire of roughly 2,530 m in the Sea to Sky region north of Whistler, near Gold Bridge and Bralorne, just south of Mount Sloan. It is a remote alpine objective with five trad routes: two at 5.6, one at 5.7 and two at 5.8. The lines follow ridges and faces rather than short crag pitches, and one face line crosses steep snow. Getting to the base takes a long traverse or ridge walk, so expect a full mountain day rather than a quick outing. Rack and rope skills for alpine terrain matter more here than sport-crag fitness.

bc_manzanita_wall.blurb: Manzanita Wall is a sport crag in the Chinese Mountains on Quadra Island, a short ferry hop from Campbell River. It stands about 30 m tall and has a curved, steep-but-not-vertical face. Five sport routes run from 5.7 up through 5.9, with three of them at 5.9, so it suits newer leaders and anyone wanting a warm-up before harder neighbours. It is among the crags nearest the trailhead lot, which keeps the walk short. Sections of the left side need a scramble to a ledge before the first moves.

bc_main_wall_left_portion.blurb: The left half of the Main Wall sits at Kitselas, in the hills outside Terrace in northern British Columbia. It is a single-pitch granite wall mixing crack lines with slabs. Five routes cover top-rope, trad and one sport line, from an easy 5.4 up to a lone 5.10, with most in the 5.6 to 5.8 range. Because the cracks take natural gear and the slabs reward careful footwork, it works for beginners learning to place pro as well as groups wanting top-rope laps. A walk-off trail leads back down, so no rappelling is needed.

bc_bugaboo_spire.blurb: Bugaboo Spire is one of the main summits of the Bugaboos in the Purcell Mountains, standing above 3,000 m between two glaciers. Its steep, almost blank east face is a landmark from the campground in the valley. There are five alpine and trad routes, from 5.6 up to 5.11, including long ridge lines and some face climbing. Most routes begin from the Crescent Glacier, a straightforward walk from the hut, while others start from the col shared with Snowpatch Spire. The easiest line doubles as the usual way down. Expect glacier travel, a long day and committing terrain.

bc_sunset_slab.blurb: Sunset Slab is a low-angle sport crag in the Chinese Mountains on Quadra Island, reached by a roughly 20-minute walk up the Beech's Mountain path. It sits beneath Evening Wall on the lower side of that path and is split into a taller left section and a shorter right section. Five sport routes, graded 5.7 and 5.8, make it a good pick for climbers building confidence on friction and small holds. The rock is largely solid. Pack gear is usually left at the top before dropping down to the base.
